name: Do garage interior finishes in the Denver metro area require fire-rated drywall?

mainEntity.name: Do garage interior finishes in the Denver metro area require fire-rated drywall?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Colorado communities like Aurora, Denver, and Centennial, garages attached to homes must comply with building codes requiring a continuous fire barrier along walls and ceilings shared with living spaces. This generally involves installing 5/8-inch Type X fire-rated drywall, sealed seams, and a self-closing, solid-core or fire-rated door leading into the residence. If electrical circuits or gas line heating are added, local municipal building permits are typically required. Working with an experienced finish contractor ensures framing, drywall thickness, and penetrations meet local fire separation standards.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, building codes require fire-rated drywall on walls and ceilings shared with living spaces to create a safe barrier between the garage and home.
